auditor.role: source investigator and branch-2 proposal author; not an independent final proof or novelty certifier
auditor.independence_limitation: The same agent authored explorer branch 2. This source review may inform a fresh independent verifier but cannot serve as the final independent proof, priority, or novelty attestation.

cutoff: Sources and indexes retrieved through 2026-09-08; bounded review only.
candidate_statement_reviewed: For every integer a,b,c >= 3 and p >= 1, if G=K_{a,b,c} join K_p, then adding any missing edge inside any minimum-cardinality non-singleton part strictly decreases simple-random-walk Kemeny's constant.

scoped_verdict.summary: The exact all-p unequal-three-part strict sign statement was not located. Hu-Kirkland 2019 already gives the exact general edge-addition identity and proves adjacent subfamilies, while its Conjecture 3.4.7 leaves the relevant three-nonsingleton-part existential conclusion conjectural. Later inspected primary works do not state the candidate or a stronger sign conclusion. A valid candidate proof would therefore be a new sign analysis built on the 2019 identity, not a new general Kemeny edge-addition formula; this bounded search does not establish publication priority or novelty.

convention_alignment.graph: K_{a,b,c} join K_p is the source's complete multipartite graph with three parts of sizes a,b,c and p singleton parts; the p clique vertices are dominating.
convention_alignment.kemeny: Use the 2019 convention for the simple random walk T=D^{-1}A: kappa(T)=sum_{i=2}^n 1/(1-lambda_i). The source also writes the random-target hitting-time expression as kappa+1 because its diagonal first-passage entries are mean return times.
convention_alignment.sign: Hu-Kirkland 2019 defines Braess as strict increase and non-Braess as weak nonincrease. The candidate's strict decrease is unambiguous and stronger than merely non-Braess.
convention_alignment.later_convention_warning: Breen-deBlieck-Vander Meulen 2026 uses >= in its introductory Braess-edge wording, whereas Hu-Kirkland 2019 uses >. Compare displayed deltas and explicit strict inequalities, not the bare word Braess, across these sources.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF p.3, lines 88-104 of the page-marked text
source_comparisons.source_result: Braess means kappa(G+e)>kappa(G); non-Braess means kappa(G+e)<=kappa(G).
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: Fixes the sign convention. Candidate asserts the strictly stronger negative sign.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF pp.10-12, especially Theorem 3.2.3 on p.12; page-marked lines 507-523 and 699-714
source_comparisons.source_result: An exact formula for kappa after adding an edge between two vertices in any selected part of size at least 3 of an arbitrary complete multipartite graph.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: Foundational and more general as an identity. It does not itself give the candidate's minimum-part sign. The candidate requires a separate inequality proof after substituting the three nonsingleton sizes and p singleton parts.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF pp.13-14, Theorem 3.3.1 and proof; page-marked lines 826-909
source_comparisons.source_result: For r>=3, no singleton parts, and every part size at least 3, choosing a smallest part yields a strictly negative displayed bound for the inserted edge, although the theorem statement calls it non-Braess.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: Exact boundary analogue at p=0 and the same minimum-part strategy, but outside the candidate's p>=1 domain.

source_comparisons.source_result: For p>=1 and minimum nonsingleton part size exactly 2, a non-Braess edge exists.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: Different size regime; it does not cover a,b,c>=3.

source_comparisons.source_result: For fixed nonsingleton part sizes at least 3, there is a threshold p0 beyond which a non-Braess edge exists; the proof obtains a negative leading term in p.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: Covers only sufficiently large p and supplies neither an all-p result nor the candidate's uniform minimum-part statement.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF p.18, Theorem 3.4.4 and Corollary 3.4.5; page-marked lines 1126-1161
source_comparisons.source_result: When at least three nonsingleton parts all have the same size k>=3, every missing edge is non-Braess for every p>=1. The proof's strictly negative coefficients imply a strict decrease under the paper's positive-denominator reduction.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: Establishes the equal-size subfamily a=b=c, and is stronger there because it covers every part. It does not cover unequal a,b,c. The strictness sentence is this reviewer's inference from the displayed proof, not the corollary's wording.

source_comparisons.source_result: For complete multipartite graphs with p dominating vertices and all nonsingleton parts of size at least 3, the paper conjectures that a Braess graph can occur only with two nonsingleton parts satisfying its stated inequality.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: The candidate's weak existential consequence proves the r=3, all-p portion of this conjecture; its located strict-decrease conclusion is stronger. The source labels the encompassing statement a conjecture, not a theorem.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF p.3, Theorems 2.1-2.2; PDF p.11, Corollary 4.1
source_comparisons.source_result: Adding an edge between two newly attached or existing pendent twins gives a Braess increase for every nontrivial connected base graph.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: Different graph operation and opposite sign; it cites the 2019 complete-multipartite work but does not extend its dominated multipartite sign results.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF pp.1-2, Introduction and roadmap; PDF p.6, Theorem 3.10
source_comparisons.source_result: Studies the edge joining endpoints of twin pendent paths at a cut vertex and gives a criterion for that operation.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: The introduction only summarizes Hu-Kirkland's complete-multipartite characterization; the paper's theorems concern a different cut-vertex family.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF pp.1-2, Abstract and Introduction, especially page-marked lines 55-85
source_comparisons.source_result: Enumerates and bounds Braess edges in families of trees, including paths, spiders, and brooms.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: It describes Hu-Kirkland as the complete-multipartite source and then explicitly restricts its own purpose to trees.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF p.1, Abstract; PDF pp.3-4, page-marked lines 101-155; Theorems 3.1 and 4.1
source_comparisons.source_result: Provides attainable maximum increase and decrease bounds when one edge is added to an initial tree, with extremal trees and edges.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: Despite its broad title, the main results are tree-only and do not cover the dense complete-multipartite target.

source_comparisons.locator: PDF pp.11-12, Theorem 3.5 and Remark 3.6; page-marked lines 723-865
source_comparisons.source_result: Gives a general exact formula for adding a clique to an independent set of twin vertices, expressed through degree, edge count, and accessibility index.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: A broader later mechanism, but not a sign classification. For two vertices it still requires evaluating and bounding the target graph's accessibility index.

source_comparisons.source_result: Classifies Braess clique insertion in complete bipartite graphs; k=2 recovers the earlier complete-bipartite edge criterion.
source_comparisons.relation_to_candidate: The section applies the general formula only to two partite sets, not three nonsingleton parts plus p singleton parts. The paper's conclusion proposes further work on families with large independent sets rather than stating the target theorem.

direct_corollary_assessment.reason: No inspected theorem covers unequal a,b,c, every p>=1, and the strict sign in a minimum nonsingleton part. Theorem 3.2.3 reduces the question to algebra but does not discharge it. The branch's proposed positivity decomposition is therefore a substantive sign argument, not merely a citation or parameter renaming.
direct_corollary_assessment.reuse_requirement: Any eventual proof must foreground Hu-Kirkland Theorem 3.2.3 as the exact starting identity and claim only the resulting sign theorem/corollary.

recommended_frozen_statement: Let a,b,c,p be integers with a,b,c>=3 and p>=1, and let G=K_{a,b,c} join K_p. Put m=min{a,b,c}. For every nonsingleton part S of G with |S|=m and every distinct u,v in S, K(G+uv)-K(G)<0, where K is Kemeny's constant of the simple random walk T=D^{-1}A.
recommended_claim_boundaries: State every tied minimum part, not just one relabelled representative; within-part pair invariance follows from graph automorphisms but should be said explicitly.
State strict delta <0 instead of relying on the convention-sensitive words Braess or non-Braess.
Describe the existential consequence as the r=3 portion of Hu-Kirkland Conjecture 3.4.7, and the strict/location result as a strengthening within that portion.
Do not describe the exact edge-addition formula as new; it is Theorem 3.2.3 of Hu-Kirkland 2019, with a later accessibility-index reformulation in Breen et al. 2026.
Do not claim resolution for four or more nonsingleton parts, classification of all edge signs, publication priority, global novelty, or an open problem from this bounded search.

search_evidence.citation_index_observation: At retrieval, Crossref reported 5 citations, OpenAlex 7, and Semantic Scholar returned 8 records including one malformed journal-title record. The August 2026 clique preprint was present in Semantic Scholar but absent from OpenAlex's citing list. These services are discovery aids only and demonstrably incomplete/inconsistent here.
search_evidence.arxiv_query_observation: The bounded exact phrase query for Braess edge returned four arXiv records; the Kemeny plus multipartite query returned zero. Neither result is evidence of absence outside that index or of novelty.

limitations: This is a bounded primary-source and forward-citation review, not a systematic review of every journal, thesis, preprint server, language, or unpublished manuscript.
Citation databases can miss or mislink citations; their count disagreement is retained rather than reconciled into a false complete census.
The review does not certify the branch proof. It assesses only source relationship and priority risk.

Failure to locate the theorem is not evidence that no prior proof exists. Publication priority, novelty, and current openness remain unresolved until a broader expert literature review and normal scholarly scrutiny.
